description: New York delta checked against dmv.ny.gov point and alcohol pages.

questions.q: In New York, Driving While Intoxicated is a BAC of
questions.explanation: NY DMV defines DWI as 0.08 BAC or higher, or other evidence of intoxication. Commercial drivers are at 0.04.

provenance.section: Penalties for alcohol or drug-related violations

questions.q: New York may suspend a driver license at
questions.explanation: The NY DMV point-system page states that 11 points in 24 months may result in a license suspension. Points are counted from the violation date.

provenance.section: The New York State driver point system

questions.q: A New York junior license or learner permit is not valid for driving alone in
questions.explanation: A junior license is not valid in the five boroughs of New York City at all. A junior learner permit may be used there only from 5 a.m. to 9 p.m. with a qualified supervising driver, and never from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m.

questions.q: Using a hand-held phone while driving in New York
options: Is allowed if traffic is stopped
Is a traffic infraction worth 5 points
questions.explanation: The NY Driver's Manual (ch. 8): it is a traffic infraction to speak into or listen to a hand-held phone while driving; a first offense can bring a fine up to $200 and five license points.

questions.q: In New York, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: New York issues a learner's permit for a car at 16 years at the earliest.

questions.q: In New York, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: New York requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in New York complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: New York requires 50 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

questions.q: Of a New York teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: New York requires at least 15 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.

questions.q: In New York, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In New York, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16½ years.

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in New York not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: New York restricts provisional drivers from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.

provenance.manual: The Graduated License Law | NY DMV

questions.q: In New York, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: New York drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 17 years.

questions.q: How many questions are on the New York car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The New York car knowledge test has 20 questions.

provenance.manual: New York State Driver's Manual and Practice Tests

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the New York car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 70% to pass the New York car knowledge test.

provenance.manual: New York State Driver's Manual and Practice Tests

questions.q: In New York, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In New York, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.

questions.q: In New York, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: New York sets the under-21 limit at 0.02%.

provenance.manual: Penalties for Alcohol or Drug-Related Violations | NY DMV

questions.q: In New York, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in New York brings a suspension of 1 year.

provenance.manual: Penalties for Alcohol or Drug-Related Violations | NY DMV

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in New York?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in New York can be posted up to 65 mph for cars.

provenance.manual: Chapter 10: Special Driving Conditions | NY DMV

questions.q: Which best describes New York's law on drivers using a phone?
options: No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
Only texting is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
questions.explanation: New York: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

provenance.manual: Cell Phone Use and Texting | NY DMV

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in New York?
options: Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In New York, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.

questions.q: How is New York's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
No seat belt law for adults
questions.explanation: New York seat belt enforcement is primary.

provenance.manual: NY DMV (page saved by the owner)

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in New York?
questions.explanation: New York requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.

provenance.manual: NY DMV (page saved by the owner)

questions.q: What is New York's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: New York requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $10,000.
